sanskrit: paidvasya manmahe vayaṃ sthirasya sthiradhāmnaḥ | ime paścāt pṛdākavaḥ pradīdhyata āsate ||
english: We meditate upon Paidva, the steadfast one, the firmly-abiding one; these spotted serpents behind us sit blazing forth.

sanskrit: naṣṭāsavo naṣṭaviṣā hatā indreṇa vajriṇā | jaghānendro jaghnimā vayam ||
english: Their life-breath extinguished, their venom destroyed, slain by Indra the wielder of the vajra — Indra has struck them down; we likewise have struck them down.

sanskrit: hatās tiraścirājayo nipiṣṭāsaḥ pṛdākavaḥ | darviṃ karikrataṃ śvitraṃ darbheṣv asitaṃ jahi ||
english: Slain are the tiraścirāja serpents, crushed are the spotted pṛdākus; strike down the darvī, the karikrata, the śvitra, the dark asita lurking in the kuśa-grass.

sanskrit: kairātikā kumārikā sakhā khanati bheṣajam | hiraṇyayībhir abhribhir girīṇām upa sānuṣu ||
english: A Kirāta maiden, a young girl companion, digs up the healing herb with her golden spades upon the ridges of the mountains.

sanskrit: āyam agan yuvā bhiṣak pṛśnihāparājitaḥ | sa vai svajasya jambhana ubhayor vṛścikasya ca ||
english: Here has come the young healer, the variegated, the unvanquished; he is indeed the crusher of the svaja serpent and of both species of scorpion.

sanskrit: indro me 'hīn ajambhayan mitraś ca varuṇaś ca | vātāparjanyobhā ||
english: Indra has crushed the serpents for me, and Mitra and Varuṇa, and both Vāta and Parjanya.

sanskrit: paidvo me 'hīn ajambhayat pṛdākūṃś ca pṛdākvaḥ | svajān tiraścirājīn kasarṇīlān daśonaśīn ||
english: Paidva has crushed the serpents for me, and the spotted pṛdākus as well — the svajas, the tiraścirājas, the kasarṇīlas, the daśonaśīs.

sanskrit: indro jaghāna prathamo janitāram ahe tava | teṣāṃ vas tṛhyamāṇānāṃ kaḥ svit teṣām asad rasaḥ ||
english: Indra first slew the progenitor of your kind, O serpent; of those crushed ones, what then could remain as the essence of them?

sanskrit: saṃ hi śīrṣāṇy agrabhaṃ pauñjiṣṭa iva karvaram | sindhor madhyaṃ paretya vy anijam aher viṣam ||
english: For I have seized the heads together, as Pauñjiṣṭa seizes the skull-bowl; having crossed to the midst of the Sindhu river, I wash away the serpent's venom.

sanskrit: ahīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ viṣaṃ parā vahantu sindhavaḥ | hatās tiraścirājayo nipiṣṭāsaḥ pṛdākavaḥ ||
english: Let the rivers carry away the venom of all serpents; slain are the tiraścirājas, crushed are the spotted pṛdākus.

sanskrit: oṣadhīnām ahaṃ vṛṇa urvarīr iva sādhuyā | nayāmy arvatīr iva- -ahe nir aitu te viṣam ||
english: I choose out the herbs, as one chooses fertile fields with skill; I lead them like swift mares — O serpent, let your venom go forth out of you.

sanskrit: yad agnau sūrye viṣaṃ pṛthivyām oṣadhīṣu yat | kāndāviṣaṃ kaniklakaṃ nir aitv aitu te vahiḥ ||
english: Whatever venom is in fire, in the sun, in the earth, in the herbs — the kāndā-venom, the kanikla — let it go forth; let it become your secretion flowing outward.

sanskrit: aṅgādaṅgāt pra cyāvaya hṛdayaṃ pari varjaya | adhā viṣasya yat tejo avācīnaṃ tad etu te ||
english: Drive it out from limb to limb, protect the heart from it; then let the fiery power of the venom depart downward from you.

sanskrit: agne trāyasva vimadaṃ nayemaṃ punar dhehi jīvase jātavedaḥ | mā te heḍāṃsi duritāva ganma māhir vadhīd viṣataḥ puruṣaṃ naḥ ||
english: O Agni, protect Vimada; lead this one back, restore him to life, O Jātavedas. May we not fall into your wrath through wrongdoing; let not the serpent slay our man with its venom.

sanskrit: ye agnijā oṣadhijā ahīnāṃ ye abhrajā vidyuta ā babhūvuḥ | teṣāṃ jātāni bahudhā bahūni tebhyaḥ sarpebhyo namasā vidhema ||
english: Those serpents born of fire, born of herbs, those that have come into being from clouds and lightning — their many and diverse broods: to those serpents we would offer reverence.

sanskrit: taudī nāmāsi kanyā ghṛtācī nāma vā asi | adhaspadena te pador ā dade viṣadūṣaṇam ||
english: You are named Taudī, or else you are named Ghṛtācī, O maiden; from beneath your foot, from between your feet, I take the venom-antidote.

sanskrit: āre abhūd viṣam araud viṣe viṣam aprāg api | agnir aher nir adhāg viṣaṃ somo nir aṇayīt | daṃṣṭāram anv agād viṣam ahir amṛta ||
english: The venom stood far off; venom wailed at venom and shrank away; Agni drove out the venom of the serpent, Soma led it away; the venom followed after the biter — the serpent became deathless.

sanskrit: kutas tau jātau katamaḥ so ardhaḥ kasmāl lokāt katarasyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ | vatsau virājaḥ salilād udaitāṃ tau tvā pṛcchāmi katareṇa dugdhā ||
english: Whence were those two born? Which is that half? From which realm, from which of the two earths? The two calves of Virāj arose from the primordial waters — I ask you: by which of the two was she milked?

sanskrit: yo 'krandayat salilaṃ mahitvā yoniṃ kṛtvā tribhujaṃ śayānam | vatsaḥ kāmadugho virājo guhā cakre tanvaḥ parācīḥ ||
english: He who made the waters cry out by his greatness, having fashioned a triangular womb lying there — the wish-fulfilling calf of Virāj has made the bodies turn away from sight in the hidden depths.

sanskrit: yāni catvāri bṛhanti yeṣāṃ caturthaṃ viyunakti vācam | brahmainad vidyāt tapasā vipaścid yasminn ekaṃ yujyate yasminn ekam ||
english: Those four great ones, of which the fourth releases speech — let the wise brahman know this through ascetic power: that in which the one is yoked, and that in which the one alone abides.

sanskrit: bṛhataḥ pari sāmāni ṣaṣṭhāt pañcādhi nirmitā | bṛhad bṛhatyā nirmitaṃ kuto 'dhi bṛhatī mitā ||
english: The sāmans are fashioned around the Bṛhat; from the sixth, five are built above it; the Bṛhat is fashioned from the Bṛhatī meter — from what, moreover, is the Bṛhatī measured out?

sanskrit: bṛhatī pari mātrāyā mātur mātrādhi nirmitā | māyā hi jajñe māyāyā māyāyā mātalī pari ||
english: The Bṛhatī is fashioned around the measure, built upon the mother's measure; for Māyā was born from Māyā, and Mātali arose from Māyā.

sanskrit: vaiśvānarasya pratimopari dyaur yāvad rodasī vibabādhe agniḥ | tataḥ ṣaṣṭhād āmuto yanti stomā ud ito yanty abhi ṣaṣṭham ahnaḥ ||
english: Above the image of Vaiśvānara is the sky; as far as Agni has pressed apart the two world-halves — from thence, from the sixth, the stotra-hymns proceed; they rise up hence toward the sixth day.

sanskrit: ṣaṭ ṭvā pṛcchāma ṛṣayaḥ kaśyapedaṃ tvaṃ hi yuktaṃ yuyukṣe yogyaṃ ca | virājam āhur brahmaṇaḥ pitaraṃ tāṃ no vi dhehy ṛtuthā sakhibhyaḥ ||
english: We seers, six of us, ask you this, O Kaśyapa — for you have harnessed what is fit to be harnessed and what is capable of yoking; they call Virāj the father of Brahman — reveal her to us according to the seasons, among our companions.

sanskrit: yāṃ pracyutām anu yajñāḥ pracyuvanta upatiṣṭhanta upatiṣṭhamānām | tasyā vraje prasave yakṣam ejati sā virāḍ ṛṣayaḥ parame vyoman ||
english: She when dislodged, the sacrifices were dislodged after her; she when standing firm, they stand firm in attendance upon her; in her cowpen, at her bringing-forth, the yakṣa trembles — she is Virāj, O seers, in the highest heaven.

sanskrit: aprāṇaiti prāṇena prāṇatīnāṃ virāṭ svarājam abhy eti paścāt | viśvaṃ mṛśantīm abhirūpāṃ virājaṃ paśyanti tve na tve paśyanty enām ||
english: The breathless one advances through the breath of breathing beings; Virāj follows after Svarāj from behind; Virāj, touching all things, beautiful in form — some see her in you, others see her not in you.

sanskrit: ko virājo mithunatvaṃ pra veda ka ṛtūn ka u kalpam asyāḥ | kramān ko asyā bahudhā vidugdhān ko asyā dhāma katidhā vyuṣṭīḥ ||
english: Who truly knows the twofold nature of Virāj, who knows her seasons, who again knows her ordered pattern? Who knows her strides, drawn forth in manifold ways, who knows her abode and how manifold are her dawns?
